title: Best Pair of Viewpoints
statement:
Along a trail there are viewpoints at positions `0, 1, 2, ...`; viewpoint `i` has a beauty of `values[i]`. If you visit viewpoint `i` and later viewpoint `j` (`i < j`), the pair scores `values[i] + values[j] + i - j`: the two beauties, minus the distance you have to walk between them.

Return the largest score of any pair.

hints.nudge: Split the score into two parts: one that only depends on i, and one that only depends on j.
hints.pattern: score = (values[i] + i) + (values[j] - j): keep the best (values[i] + i) seen so far while you walk to the right.
hints.pseudocode:
best_left = values[0] + 0; answer = -infinity
for j in 1..n-1:
  answer = max(answer, best_left + values[j] - j)
  best_left = max(best_left, values[j] + j)
return answer
hints.walkthrough: Trying all pairs is O(n^2). Rewrite the score as (values[i] + i) + (values[j] - j). For a fixed j the second part is fixed, so you want the largest possible first part among all i before j. Sweep j from left to right and carry `best_left`, the largest values[i] + i seen so far (before j). At each j compute best_left + values[j] - j, keep the maximum, and only afterwards add j itself to the candidates for later positions (a pair needs i < j). One pass, O(n) time, O(1) memory.
